correctness.rationale: For nonempty vertex-transitive simple graphs, the three-move Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé winning criterion is equality of all possible distinct-ordered-pair edge indicators and sets of third-vertex adjacency patterns. The first chosen vertex can be matched by transitivity, the second determines a pair profile, and the third can be matched exactly when its four-bit extension mask is present. For Johnson k-sets, intersection distance d=1,2,≥3 gives the claimed edge/nonedge masks by exchanging elements of I=A∩B, X=A\B, Y=B\A and Z=ground\(A∪B). The unique disjoint k=3,n=6 exception is a pigeonhole obstruction to a third vertex nonadjacent to both; with n≥7 an extra element supplies one. For k=2 the outside-element thresholds are n=5 and n=6; k=1 complete-graph threshold is n=3. Independent brute-force subset enumeration checked masks and seven distinct profiles in representative bounded cases. The arbitrary-size assertion follows from the constructive proof, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: No higher-quantifier-rank, counting or metric-betweenness claims.
